You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0288.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

ls -la; python - <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
print('rdkit ok')
PY

args.command:
cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, rdMolDescriptors
from rdkit.Geometry import Point3D
import numpy as np
# Heavy atoms numbered by positions in the supplied drawing
pts=[(128,284),(232,224),(292,121),(396,181),(336,284),(336,405),(231,465),(128,405),(231,585),(336,645),(439,585),(439,465),(553,428),(623,526),(553,625),(623,332),(738,366),(738,487),(842,547),(946,487),(946,366),(842,306),(842,667),(946,727),(1050,667),(1050,547),(1154,487),(1258,547),(1258,667),(1154,727),(1361,727),(23,223),(480,154),(584,215),(445,91),(507,93),(738,604),(842,430),(1048,428),(1363,487),(1465,667),(1361,846)]
oxygen={29,33,38,39}
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for i in range(len(pts)):
    a=Chem.Atom('O' if i in oxygen else ('N' if i==14 else 'C'))
    if i==14:
        a.SetNumExplicitHs(1)
    rw.AddAtom(a)
single=[(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4),(4,1),(4,5),(6,7),(7,0),
(12,15),(15,16),(16,17),(17,13),(16,21),(21,20),(20,19),(19,18),(18,17),
(18,22),(22,23),(23,24),(24,25),(25,19),(26,27),(27,28),(28,29),(29,24),
(28,30),(30,40),(3,32),(32,33),(33,15),(32,34),(32,35),(17,36),(18,37),(19,38),(27,39)]
double=[(0,31),(25,26),(30,41)]
aromatic=[(5,6),(6,8),(8,9),(9,10),(10,11),(11,5),(11,12),(12,13),(13,14),(14,10)]
for pairs,btyp in [(single,Chem.BondType.SINGLE),(double,Chem.BondType.DOUBLE),(aromatic,Chem.BondType.AROMATIC)]:
    for i,j in pairs: rw.AddBond(i,j,btyp)
# Hydrogen atoms which are drawn as wedge/dash substituents
explicit_H={1:(184,179),4:(410,305),16:(738,294),24:(1050,750)}
hidx={}
for i,p in explicit_H.items():
    j=rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom('H')); hidx[i]=j; pts.append(p); rw.AddBond(i,j,Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
m=rw.GetMol(); Chem.SanitizeMol(m)
conf=Chem.Conformer(m.GetNumAtoms()); conf.Set3D(False)
for i,(x,y) in enumerate(pts): conf.SetAtomPosition(i,Point3D(x/100,-y/100,0))
m.AddConformer(conf)
wedges=[(1,hidx[1],False),(3,32,False),(4,hidx[4],False),(15,33,True),(16,hidx[16],True),(17,36,False),(18,37,True),(19,38,False),(24,hidx[24],False),(27,39,True),(28,30,True)]
# Reorient each wedge bond to start at the stereogenic center.
rw=Chem.RWMol(m)
for i,j,solid in wedges:
    b=rw.GetBondBetweenAtoms(i,j)
    if b.GetBeginAtomIdx()!=i:
        rw.RemoveBond(i,j);rw.AddBond(i,j,Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
    rw.GetBondBetweenAtoms(i,j).SetBondDir(Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE if solid else Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH)
m=rw.GetMol()
Chem.AssignChiralTypesFromBondDirs(m,replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m,cleanIt=True,force=True)
print('Formula',rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(m))
print('SMILES',Chem.MolToSmiles(m))
for i,j,w in wedges:
    a=m.GetAtomWithIdx(i);print(i,a.GetChiralTag(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode') if a.HasProp('_CIPCode') else '-')
Chem.MolToMolFile(m,'drawing.mol')
# Atom-numbered visualization of the constructed topology and stereochemistry.
from rdkit.Chem.Draw import rdMolDraw2D
draw=rdMolDraw2D.MolDraw2DCairo(1500,1000)
draw.drawOptions().addAtomIndices=True
draw.drawOptions().bondLineWidth=2
draw.DrawMolecule(m)
draw.FinishDrawing()
open('graph.png','wb').write(draw.GetDrawingText())
# Add every hydrogen, discard drawing coordinates, and find relaxed 3D conformers.
m.RemoveAllConformers()
m=Chem.AddHs(m)
params=AllChem.ETKDGv3(); params.randomSeed=288; params.numThreads=0; params.pruneRmsThresh=0.3
ids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(m,numConfs=80,params=params)
print('Conformers',len(ids),flush=True)
res=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(m,numThreads=0,maxIters=1500)
energies=[(en,i,status) for i,(status,en) in zip(ids,res)]
energies.sort()
print('Best energies',energies[:10],flush=True)
energy,cid,status=energies[0]
# Validate that 3D stereochemistry matches every assigned center.
check=Chem.Mol(m)
Chem.AssignStereochemistryFrom3D(check,confId=cid,replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(check,cleanIt=True,force=True)
for i,j,w in wedges:
    a=m.GetAtomWithIdx(i);b=check.GetAtomWithIdx(i)
    assert a.GetChiralTag()==b.GetChiralTag(), (i,a.GetChiralTag(),b.GetChiralTag())
conf=m.GetConformer(cid)
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:
    f.write(f'{m.GetNumAtoms()}\nAll-atom 3D structure reconstructed from mol_0288.png; angstrom\n')
    for a in m.GetAtoms():
        p=conf.GetAtomPosition(a.GetIdx())
        f.write(f'{a.GetSymbol()} {p.x:.8f} {p.y:.8f} {p.z:.8f}\n')
Chem.MolToMolFile(m,'answer.mol',confId=cid)
print('Wrote answer.xyz:',m.GetNumAtoms(),'atoms')
PY
python build.py

test -f answer.xyz && head -n 5 answer.xyz && python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('answer.xyz')
a=p.read_text().splitlines()
assert len(a)==int(a[0])+2
print(f'Confirmed: {p.name}, {a[0]} atoms, {p.stat().st_size} bytes')
